title: What the Fire Leaves
logline: A family sows a paddy field, tends it through drought and pests, and waits to see whether the season ends in harvest or in ruin.
human_question: How many different forces have to go right, one after another, for anything to come to fruit?

situation.what_happens: A farming family works one full season: preparing and sowing, keeping water to the field, feeding and watching the crop, guarding it at night, and meeting whatever comes, a dry spell, a pest, a price collapse. At the end there is a harvest, a partial harvest or a loss, and the family's year is decided by it.
situation.who_is_involved: The household who farm the land and carry the loan; the labourers who are paid by the day; the buyers who set the price; and the neighbours who share water and equipment.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A year's income, the loan taken against the crop, and whether the family keeps farming.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A season has a fixed calendar and an unfixed outcome. Setbacks are cumulative, and one of them can end the crop outright while others only reduce it. Reality decides the harvest; the film cannot know it in advance and must not need any particular ending.

concept_merge.why_together: One concept. Kamma by function (C055) separates what starts a result, what keeps it going, what wears it down and what cuts it off, and the source's own picture of the four is a farming season: seed sown, the crop tended, a drought that weakens it, a fire that ends it.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That an outcome is the product of several forces acting on each other over time, which is the opposite of a single cause and the opposite of fate. The source names the forces and gives nobody a way to read them in any particular person's situation.

concept_links.why: The source's own image for the four functions is exactly this season: sowing, tending, drought, fire [C055-P:L127]. The digest is explicit that this must not become 'everything happens for a reason' or 'they deserved it', and that the source's examples of illness and poverty describe how forces interact rather than licensing any judgement of real people's suffering.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: The texts describe results as produced by several forces at once, one starting something, another supporting it, another wearing it down and another ending it, and they give nobody a way to read those forces in a real person's life.
what_must_be_real: A real family's real season with its real financial stakes, and no foreknowledge of the outcome. No hardship is presented as deserved.
position_hint: middle, if it were kept: a season-long observational film whose concept is already carried by a kept idea.
risks: Turning a family's crop loss into a moral lesson
Implying that hardship reflects the family's own past actions
A season-long schedule that the production may not be able to hold
drop_if: No family will commit to being filmed across a whole season
The season is too uneventful, or too catastrophic, to film honestly

connections.note: Folded into the film about a volunteer doing the opposing good, which now carries the whole set of four functions, the source's own field image, and this idea's situation: a year on a fixed calendar with an unfixed outcome, carried by people whose living depends on it.
Both are growing seasons whose outcome the film cannot know; the community-scale season is the one that keeps an episode.

selection.reason: Its concept is carried by a kept idea and its situation overlaps the kept drought film; folding it in completes the four functions in the kept idea and gives them a season to be observed in.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
